### When Waking Feels Easy

Timing and ease are different questions. Late in the night, deep slow-wave sleep usually becomes less common, while lighter NREM sleep and REM sleep take up more of the cycle. Waking from these stages may cause less sleep inertia than waking from deep N3 sleep. That can make a pre-alarm awakening feel natural, without fixing its exact minute.

### Practice May Matter

Practice may matter too. In a home study of 11 students who did not already have a self-awakening habit, 82% succeeded by the seventh day when trying to wake at their usual time without an alarm. In a separate survey of 643 students, 66 reported the habit and kept sleep and wake times about 30 minutes earlier. This observational link suggests that consistency and expectation may help.

## In one line

A wake-up that feels like a private appointment may reflect preparation, practice, and a forgiving margin of biology—not a clock hidden in the brain.
